messages:
rachel_k: Hey folks, first-week setup weirdness. I followed the README, ran docker-compose, but the Postgres container fails to create the socket with `initdb: could not create directory \"/var/run/postgresql\": Permission denied`. I'm on macOS and the compose mounts `./pg_run:/var/run/postgresql` because I thought it would let my host app talk via unix socket. Any safe workarounds?

tom_s: Welcome @rachel_k! Quick note: binding container runtime dirs like /var/run into host mounts on Docker Desktop (mac) often breaks because gRPC FUSE / osxfs restricts certain socket operations. We generally avoid mounting /var/run.

rachel_k: Ah — I did that to reuse the socket. Is there a way to preserve socket-based local dev without changing the repo to use TCP?

mira: Two pragmatic paths: 1) Switch to TCP remapped ports for host dev (e.g., 54320:5432 and update .env.local), which is the least flaky. 2) Run the web app inside compose so it can use the container-local unix socket (not mounted to host). We avoid mounting /var/run on mac because permission bits and ephemeral sockets don't survive the mount.

infra-bot: Tip: onboarding doc has a section on "socket vs TCP" and mac caveats: https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services#sockets

rachel_k: I prefer host dev for fast reloads. If I switch to remapped ports, what's the minimal .env change?

tom_s: Add a `.env.local` (gitignored) with `DATABASE_URL=postgres://redwood:pass@localhost:54320/redwood_dev` and in compose map `- "54320:5432"`. For Redis similarly `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:63790` and `- "63790:6379"`. That keeps your host processes talking to localhost.

mira: If you need a small helper: we have `scripts/dev-proxy.sh` that detects mac and rewrites envs temporarily to remapped ports then runs your dev server. Avoids checking in changes.

rachel_k: Good to know. For completeness — if someone insists on mounting sockets, any permission trick?

tom_s: You can try creating the host dir beforehand with correct uid/gid and allow Docker to create the socket there: `mkdir -p ./pg_run && sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pg_run` (999 often postgres uid). But on mac Docker Desktop the uid mapping is different and gRPC FUSE will still block socket creation sometimes. Not reliable.

mira: Also note: mounting the socket path can cause the container to skip initdb if it sees files and then fail to create runtime sockets. We avoid it unless you're on Linux host that supports unix domain mounts well.

infra-bot: Reminder: For onboarding we recommend named volumes for DB state and either running web inside compose or using remapped TCP ports for host web dev. https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services

rachel_k: Thanks all — I'll switch to remapped ports and add a `.env.local` so I don't touch the repo .env. Appreciate the pointers! :wave:
